descriptions.en: Metamodel for describing systems with a subset of ArchiMate (L0–L4), allowed relationship matrix, and Open Exchange notes. Depends on kc-base. UI traversal lives in archimate-ui-traversal. Not part of knowledge-core.
descriptions.cs: Metamodel podmnožiny ArchiMate (L0–L4), matice povolených vazeb a Open Exchange. Závisí na kc-base. UI traversal je v archimate-ui-traversal. Není součástí jádra knowledge-core.

descriptions.en: Not an ArchiMate concept. Root for tool policy data stored in this package (allowed pairs, exchange notes).
descriptions.cs: Není ArchiMate koncept. Kořen tool-policy dat v tomto package (povolené vazby, exchange poznámky).

classes.usageGuidance: Root for Lite tool-policy data in this package (allowed pairs, exchange notes). Not used in architecture diagrams.
classes.usageExamples: AllowedRelationship rows; the single ExchangeSpec entity.

descriptions.en: Lite matrix row: relationship class + source class + target class. Enforced by tools, not by KC.

classes.usageGuidance: Declares one allowed (relationship type, source class, target class) triple for tool-side matrix checks. KC does not enforce it.
classes.usageExamples: Assignment BusinessActor→BusinessRole; Serving TechnologyService→ApplicationComponent; DeployedOn ApplicationComponent→SystemSoftware.

descriptions.en: Open Exchange mapping notes for tools. Single instance iriLocal=exchange-spec.

classes.usageGuidance: Holds Open Exchange mapping notes for importers/exporters. Prefer a single instance with iriLocal=exchange-spec.
classes.usageExamples: exchange-spec with catalogVersion, exchangeFormat, and DeployedOn/Risk/views rules.

classes.usageGuidance: Abstract root of all ArchiMate Lite concepts (elements, relationships, views). Do not instantiate directly.
classes.usageExamples: Prefer a concrete subclass such as ApplicationComponent or Serving.

classes.usageGuidance: Abstract parent of structural/behavioral architecture elements. Instances are typed via instanceOf to a concrete subclass.
classes.usageExamples: BusinessService, ApplicationComponent, Node, Risk — never ArchiMateElement itself.

classes.usageGuidance: Abstract parent of relationship entities. Each relationship is its own entity with relSource and relTarget.
classes.usageExamples: Serving, Access, Flow, DeployedOn — create a relationship entity, not a free-form link.

classes.usageGuidance: Abstract parent of diagram/view constructs used to present the model.
classes.usageExamples: DiagramView, ViewNode, ViewConnection.

classes.usageGuidance: An organizational entity capable of performing behavior — the owner, unit, or external party accountable for a system or service.
classes.usageExamples: Business unit owning CRM; external payment provider; operations department; customer organization.

classes.usageGuidance: A responsibility that an actor may assume. Use for ownership and operating roles, not for technical accounts.
classes.usageExamples: Business owner; system owner; on-call operator; compliance officer.

classes.usageGuidance: An externally visible unit of business behavior offered to customers or the organization.
classes.usageExamples: Customer onboarding; invoice issuance; employee self-service; payment acceptance.

classes.usageGuidance: A sequence of business behaviors achieving a specific outcome. Use for key processes the system supports.
classes.usageExamples: Order-to-cash; claim handling; identity provisioning request; month-end close.

classes.usageGuidance: Stable area of responsibility or work. Answers 'what is this unit accountable for?' — unlike BusinessProcess, which answers 'what happens when…'. Use as the primary business-layer decomposition.
classes.usageExamples: Data Protection; Compliance Management; Customer Onboarding as a standing function (not a process run).

classes.usageGuidance: A modular, deployable application building block. At L0 model the whole system; at L2 split into frontend, backend, workers, etc.
classes.usageExamples: CRM as a whole; web frontend; API backend; batch worker; shared microservice.

classes.usageGuidance: Application behavior exposed to the environment (users or other systems).
classes.usageExamples: CreateCustomer service; SearchOrders; Authentication API capability; Reporting service.

classes.usageGuidance: A point of access where application services are made available to users or other applications.
classes.usageExamples: REST /v1/customers; customer web UI; Kafka topic OrdersIn; SOAP gateway.

classes.usageGuidance: Automated behavior internal to an application component. Prefer when modeling internal capability, not a full workflow.
classes.usageExamples: ValidateOrder; CalculateTax; HashPassword; IndexDocument.

classes.usageGuidance: An application-level workflow or batch sequence spanning one or more functions.
classes.usageExamples: Nightly settlement batch; document OCR pipeline; password-reset flow.

classes.usageGuidance: An application-level state change of interest for integration or operations.
classes.usageExamples: OrderCreated; PaymentFailed; UserLockedOut; CertificateExpiring.

classes.usageGuidance: A temporary or logical aggregation of application components cooperating as one unit.
classes.usageExamples: Checkout collaboration (cart + payment + inventory); login collaboration (UI + IdP adapter).

classes.usageGuidance: A passive structure of data meaningful to the architecture (not every table or cache entry).
classes.usageExamples: Customer master; order transactions; audit log; configuration store; search index.

classes.usageGuidance: A technology capability used by applications — databases, identity, DNS, storage, messaging, load balancing.
classes.usageExamples: PostgreSQL database service; Keycloak/IdP; corporate DNS; object storage; Kafka cluster service.

classes.usageGuidance: An access point to a technology service that is architecturally significant (stable endpoints, VIPs).
classes.usageExamples: DB listener host:5432; ingress VIP; Kubernetes API endpoint; DNS resolver address.

classes.usageGuidance: A computational resource on which artifacts and system software are deployed (logical or virtual).
classes.usageExamples: Application VM; Kubernetes worker node; bastion host; managed DB instance endpoint node.

classes.usageGuidance: A physical ICT resource. Use when the physical appliance matters for DR, network, or ownership.
classes.usageExamples: Physical server; firewall appliance; hardware load balancer; storage array controller.

classes.usageGuidance: Software environment that hosts or runs application artifacts (OS, platform, middleware, DB engine).
classes.usageExamples: RHEL; Kubernetes; PostgreSQL engine; JVM runtime; message broker runtime.

classes.usageGuidance: A physical piece of data used or produced in deployment — images, packages, charts, config bundles.
classes.usageExamples: Container image; Helm chart; Terraform module; signed config package; WAR/JAR release.

classes.usageGuidance: A communication medium or logical network segment relevant to security/DR (VLAN, subnet, WAN, DMZ). Set networkKind from infrastructure/network depth (L3+); add cidr, vlanId, and networkRole at L4.
classes.usageExamples: APP_NET VLAN 10.1.0.0/16 production; DC-WAN; DMZ; backup network.

classes.usageGuidance: A named communication path between nodes or networks for impact analysis. Use Path when the route itself matters (WAN, replication link, zoned crossing) rather than Flow (what is transferred) or Association (membership or attachment).
classes.usageExamples: DC1↔DC2 replication path; primary site to DR site WAN path; app-tier to DB-tier path spanning VLANs.

classes.usageGuidance: A physical structure or environment such as a datacenter or technical building.
classes.usageExamples: DC1 Prague; colo facility; head-office server room.

classes.usageGuidance: A geographic or organizational place. Use when site matters for DR, latency, or regulation.
classes.usageExamples: Prague; Brno DR site; EU-central region; branch office.

classes.usageGuidance: A statement of need that must be realized by the architecture (availability, RTO/RPO, compliance).
classes.usageExamples: RTO ≤ 4h; RPO ≤ 15m; 99.9% availability; GDPR retention constraint.

classes.usageGuidance: Result of an analysis used to motivate decisions (criticality, maturity, health).
classes.usageExamples: Business criticality = high; architecture fitness review; dependency risk score.

classes.usageGuidance: A risk relevant to the architecture (Risk and Security overlay). Prefer for known SPOFs and threat outcomes.
classes.usageExamples: Single WAN link between DCs; sole IdP without standby; unencrypted backup channel.

classes.usageGuidance: Difference between baseline and target architecture that a change initiative must close.
classes.usageExamples: Missing HA for payment DB; no DR runbook for IdP; absent network segmentation.

classes.usageGuidance: A series of actions designed to achieve a goal within a defined timeframe.
classes.usageExamples: CRM migration wave 1; network zoning project; HA database rollout.

classes.usageGuidance: Whole–part where the part has the same lifetime as the whole (strong ownership).
classes.usageExamples: CRM system composed of Frontend+Backend+Worker; Node composed of Devices.

classes.usageGuidance: Whole–part grouping without shared lifetime (loose collection).
classes.usageExamples: ApplicationCollaboration aggregating components; cluster aggregating nodes.

classes.usageGuidance: Allocation of responsibility or deployment: actor→role, role→service, software→node, artifact→node.
classes.usageExamples: BusinessActor→BusinessRole; SystemSoftware→Node; Artifact→Node.

classes.usageGuidance: More concrete element realizes a more abstract one (component realizes service/requirement).
classes.usageExamples: ApplicationComponent→BusinessService; ApplicationComponent→ApplicationService; Device→TechnologyService.

classes.usageGuidance: Provider serves a consumer with behavior or capability. Preferred over Used-By for Lite models.
classes.usageExamples: ApplicationService→BusinessProcess; TechnologyService→ApplicationComponent; Device→CommunicationNetwork.

classes.usageGuidance: Behavioral element accesses a data object. Set accessMode to read, write, or readWrite.
classes.usageExamples: Backend→CustomerData (readWrite); Worker→AuditLog (write); Reporting→Orders (read).

classes.usageGuidance: Transfer of information, value, or goods between elements — not a 'uses' or Serving relationship. Always set flowLabel (what flows). Use messageOrObject for the technical payload name; attach protocol/port/zone at L2–L4.
classes.usageExamples: Backend→Payment Gateway (flowLabel=Customer orders, flowKind=data, protocol=HTTPS); WAN→APP_NET (Inter-DC replication).

classes.usageGuidance: Temporal or causal triggering: source triggers target behavior.
classes.usageExamples: ApplicationEvent→ApplicationProcess; Process A triggers Process B; schedule triggers batch.

classes.usageGuidance: Generalization/specialization between elements of the same kind.
classes.usageExamples: Generic ApplicationComponent specialized as PaymentGatewayComponent.

classes.usageGuidance: Undirected structural link when no more specific relationship fits. Prefer specific types when possible.
classes.usageExamples: Requirement↔ApplicationComponent; Node↔Facility; Facility↔Location; Node↔CommunicationNetwork.

classes.usageGuidance: Motivation influence: how an assessment or risk affects a requirement or service.
classes.usageExamples: Assessment→Requirement; Risk→BusinessService.

descriptions.en: Lite convenience. Exchange tools expand to Assignment (component→system software→node, artifact→node).

classes.usageGuidance: Lite convenience for deployment. Exchange tools expand to Assignment (e.g. component→system software→node, artifact→node).
classes.usageExamples: ApplicationComponent→SystemSoftware; Artifact→Node.

classes.usageGuidance: A named diagram/viewpoint over the model. Use viewpoint to distinguish catalog, dependencies, application, technology, network.
classes.usageExamples: sys-crm catalog view; landscape dependency view; network zone view.

classes.usageGuidance: A visual node in a diagram, usually referencing an ArchiMate element via elementRef.
classes.usageExamples: Box for ApplicationComponent; container group; free-text label node.

classes.usageGuidance: A visual edge in a diagram referencing a relationship entity and its source/target view nodes.
classes.usageExamples: Line for Serving between two ViewNodes; Flow edge with bendpoints.

descriptions.en: Relationship source element (instance of ArchiMateElement or subclass).
descriptions.cs: Zdrojový prvek vztahu (instance ArchiMateElement nebo podtřídy).

properties.usageGuidance: Marks the source element of a relationship entity. Required on every ArchiMateRelationship instance.
properties.usageExamples: Serving where source is TechnologyService PostgreSQL; Access where source is Backend component.

descriptions.en: Relationship target element (instance of ArchiMateElement or subclass).
descriptions.cs: Cílový prvek vztahu (instance ArchiMateElement nebo podtřídy).

properties.usageGuidance: Marks the target element of a relationship entity. Required on every ArchiMateRelationship instance.
properties.usageExamples: Serving targeting ApplicationComponent CRM; Access targeting DataObject CustomerMaster.

descriptions.en: Declares modeling granularity for an element, e.g. catalog, dr_minimum, application_detail, infrastructure_detail, or network_detail.
descriptions.cs: Určuje granularitu modelování prvku, např. catalog, dr_minimum, application_detail, infrastructure_detail nebo network_detail.

properties.usageGuidance: Declares modeling granularity for an element (L0–L4 style). Prefer on every ArchiMateElement; shape aml-element warns if missing.
properties.usageExamples: catalog for L0 system card; dr_minimum for L1 dependencies; application_detail; infrastructure_detail; network_detail.

properties.usageGuidance: Lifecycle status of the element in the estate (planned, live, retiring, etc.).

descriptions.en: Lifecycle status of the element in the estate, e.g. production, pilot, decommissioning, or retired.
descriptions.cs: Stav životního cyklu prvku v prostředí, např. production, pilot, decommissioning nebo retired.

properties.usageGuidance: URI pointing to an authoritative external record (CMDB, ticket, docs).

descriptions.en: URI pointing to an authoritative external record such as a CMDB entry, ticket, or documentation.
descriptions.cs: URI odkazující na autoritativní externí záznam, např. položku CMDB, ticket nebo dokumentaci.

properties.usageGuidance: Which system is authoritative for this element's facts.
properties.usageExamples: ServiceNow CMDB; Terraform state; DNS IPAM; manual architecture register.

descriptions.en: Identifies which system is authoritative for this element's facts, e.g. ServiceNow CMDB or Terraform state.
descriptions.cs: Určuje, který systém je autoritativní pro fakta o tomto prvku, např. ServiceNow CMDB nebo Terraform state.

properties.usageGuidance: Business or organizational owner accountable for the element.
properties.usageExamples: Retail Operations; Head of Payments; Business unit XYZ.

descriptions.en: Business or organizational owner accountable for the element, e.g. a business unit or department head.
descriptions.cs: Obchodní nebo organizační vlastník odpovědný za prvek, např. obchodní jednotka nebo vedoucí oddělení.

properties.usageGuidance: Technical team or role responsible for running/changing the element.
properties.usageExamples: Platform team; CRM guild; DBAs; Network ops.

descriptions.en: Technical team or role responsible for running and changing the element, e.g. Platform team or DBAs.
descriptions.cs: Technický tým nebo role odpovědná za provoz a změny prvku, např. Platform team nebo DBA.

descriptions.en: Distinguishes whether a BusinessActor is a department, person, or external party.
descriptions.cs: Rozlišuje, zda je BusinessActor oddělení (department), osoba (person) nebo externí subjekt (external).

properties.usageGuidance: Distinguishes an organizational unit, a named person, and an external party on BusinessActor. Required on every BusinessActor (shape aml-business-actor). department = org unit; person = named individual; external = party outside the organization.
properties.usageExamples: department for Odbor Compliance; person for Petr Novák; external for EU Registry.

descriptions.en: Indicates who operates or owns the element: internal, external, or shared.
descriptions.cs: Určuje, kdo prvek provozuje nebo vlastní: internal (interní), external (externí) nebo shared (sdílený).

properties.usageGuidance: Who operates or owns the element: internal to the organization, an external provider, or a shared/multi-tenant service. EU registries and vendor SaaS are typically external.
properties.usageExamples: internal for CRM Backend; external for EU Registry; shared for corporate IdP.

properties.usageGuidance: Business criticality classification used for DR and prioritization.

descriptions.en: Business criticality classification used for disaster recovery and prioritization, e.g. critical, high, medium, or low.
descriptions.cs: Klasifikace obchodní kritičnosti pro DR a prioritizaci, např. critical, high, medium nebo low.

properties.usageGuidance: Recovery Time Objective for the element or system.

descriptions.en: Recovery Time Objective — maximum acceptable downtime after an incident, e.g. 4h or 15m.
descriptions.cs: Recovery Time Objective — maximální přípustná doba výpadku po incidentu, např. 4h nebo 15m.

properties.usageGuidance: Recovery Point Objective — acceptable data loss window.

descriptions.en: Recovery Point Objective — maximum acceptable data loss window, e.g. 15m, 1h, or zero with sync replication.
descriptions.cs: Recovery Point Objective — maximální přípustné okno ztráty dat, např. 15m, 1h nebo zero při synchronní replikaci.

properties.usageGuidance: Qualifies the kind of dependency expressed by a relationship (formalized enum/dependencyType).
properties.usageExamples: runtime; data; identity; network; build-time; organizational.

descriptions.en: Qualifies the kind of dependency expressed by a relationship, e.g. runtime, data, identity, network, build-time, or organizational.
descriptions.cs: Upřesňuje typ závislosti vyjádřené vztahem, např. runtime, data, identity, network, build-time nebo organizational.

descriptions.en: States whether the dependency is mandatory or optional for degraded operation.
descriptions.cs: Určuje, zda je závislost pro omezený provoz povinná (mandatory) nebo volitelná (optional).

properties.usageGuidance: Whether the dependency is mandatory or optional for degraded operation.
What limited operation remains if the dependency fails.
properties.usageExamples: read-only catalog; queue and retry; manual workaround; full outage.

descriptions.en: Describes what limited operation remains if the dependency fails, e.g. read-only catalog or manual workaround.
descriptions.cs: Popisuje, jaký omezený provoz zůstane při selhání závislosti, např. read-only katalog nebo manuální workaround.

properties.usageGuidance: Business consequence of failure of the dependency or element.
properties.usageExamples: Cannot accept orders; delayed invoicing; login unavailable.

descriptions.en: Business consequence of failure of the dependency or element, e.g. cannot accept orders or login unavailable.
descriptions.cs: Obchodní dopad selhání závislosti nebo prvku, např. nelze přijímat objednávky nebo nedostupné přihlášení.

descriptions.en: Qualifies the business meaning of an Association, e.g. reportsTo, memberOf, locatedIn, or other.
descriptions.cs: Upřesňuje obchodní význam Association, např. reportsTo, memberOf, locatedIn nebo other.

properties.usageGuidance: Qualifies the business meaning of an Association. Prefer a specific relationship type when one exists (e.g. Composition for org hierarchy). reportsTo is a reporting line between persons, not Composition. other requires relationshipNote.
properties.usageExamples: reportsTo Petr Novák → Jiri Kreuzman; memberOf Node → CommunicationNetwork; spans Path → WAN.

properties.usageGuidance: Optional free-text note on a relationship. Required when associationKind is other.
properties.usageExamples: Temporary dual-reporting during reorganization; exception approved by architecture board.

descriptions.en: Optional free-text note on a relationship; required when associationKind is other.
descriptions.cs: Volitelná textová poznámka k vztahu; povinná, pokud je associationKind other.

properties.usageGuidance: Communication protocol on interfaces, flows, or related concepts.

descriptions.en: Communication protocol used at an interface or flow, e.g. HTTPS, TCP, gRPC, or Kafka.
descriptions.cs: Komunikační protokol na rozhraní nebo toku, např. HTTPS, TCP, gRPC nebo Kafka.

properties.usageGuidance: TCP/UDP port that is architecturally significant.

descriptions.en: Architecturally significant TCP or UDP port number, e.g. 443, 5432, or 9092.
descriptions.cs: Architektonicky významné číslo TCP/UDP portu, např. 443, 5432 nebo 9092.

properties.usageGuidance: Whether an interaction is synchronous (blocking) or asynchronous.
properties.usageExamples: true for REST request/response; false for queue/event publish.

descriptions.en: Whether an interaction is synchronous (blocking request/response) or asynchronous, e.g. true for REST or false for queue publish.
descriptions.cs: Určuje, zda je interakce synchronní (blokující request/response) nebo asynchronní, např. true pro REST nebo false pro publikaci do fronty.

properties.usageGuidance: Authentication mechanism expected at an interface or flow.
properties.usageExamples: OIDC; mTLS; API key; Kerberos; none (internal only).

descriptions.en: Authentication mechanism expected at an interface or flow, e.g. OIDC, mTLS, API key, or Kerberos.
descriptions.cs: Očekávaný autentizační mechanismus na rozhraní nebo toku, např. OIDC, mTLS, API key nebo Kerberos.

properties.usageGuidance: Timeout policy relevant to resilience analysis.

descriptions.en: Timeout policy relevant to resilience analysis, e.g. 5s, 30s, or 2m.
descriptions.cs: Politika timeoutu relevantní pro analýzu odolnosti, např. 5s, 30s nebo 2m.

properties.usageGuidance: Retry/backoff expectations for a dependency.
properties.usageExamples: 3 retries exponential backoff; no retry; at-least-once with DLQ.

descriptions.en: Retry and backoff expectations for a dependency, e.g. 3 retries with exponential backoff or at-least-once with DLQ.
descriptions.cs: Očekávání opakování a backoffu u závislosti, např. 3 opakování s exponenciálním backoffem nebo at-least-once s DLQ.

properties.usageGuidance: Technical name of the message, event, or payload exchanged. On Flow this is the payload identifier; the business description belongs in flowLabel.

descriptions.en: Technical name of the message, event, or payload exchanged, e.g. OrderCreated or CustomerDTO.
descriptions.cs: Technický název zprávy, události nebo payloadu, např. OrderCreated nebo CustomerDTO.

properties.usageGuidance: Business description of what is transferred by a Flow — 'what flows'. Required on every Flow (shape aml-flow). Do not confuse with messageOrObject, which is the technical payload or event name.
properties.usageExamples: Customer orders; Inter-DC replication; Invoice PDF; Identity assertions.

descriptions.en: Business description of what is transferred by a Flow, e.g. customer orders or identity assertions.
descriptions.cs: Obchodní popis toho, co Flow přenáší, např. zákaznické objednávky nebo identity assertions.

descriptions.en: Kind of Flow transferred: data payload, event/message, control signal, or physical transfer.
descriptions.cs: Druh Flow: datová zátěž (data), událost/zpráva (event), řídicí signál (control) nebo fyzický přenos (physical).

properties.usageGuidance: Kind of Flow: data payload, event/message, control signal, or physical transfer. Use data vs event to distinguish request/response payloads from published events.
properties.usageExamples: data for API or DB query; event for Kafka OrderCreated; control for health check; physical for media or material.

descriptions.en: How a behavioral element accesses a DataObject: read, write, or readWrite.
descriptions.cs: Způsob přístupu behaviorálního prvku k DataObject: read, write nebo readWrite.

properties.usageGuidance: How a behavioral element accesses a DataObject (Access relationships).
Business/technical classification of a DataObject.

descriptions.en: Business or technical classification of a DataObject, e.g. master, transactional, audit, reference, or cache.
descriptions.cs: Obchodní nebo technická klasifikace DataObject, např. master, transactional, audit, reference nebo cache.

properties.usageGuidance: System of record that masters this data object.
properties.usageExamples: CRM; ERP; IdP; locally owned by this system.

descriptions.en: System of record that masters this data object, e.g. CRM, ERP, or IdP.
descriptions.cs: Autoritativní systém (system of record) pro tento datový objekt, např. CRM, ERP nebo IdP.

properties.usageGuidance: Retention period or policy for the data.
properties.usageExamples: 7 years; 90 days; GDPR erasure on request.

descriptions.en: Retention period or policy for the data, e.g. 7 years, 90 days, or GDPR erasure on request.
descriptions.cs: Doba nebo politika uchovávání dat, např. 7 let, 90 dní nebo výmaz dle GDPR na žádost.

properties.usageGuidance: Whether the data can be rebuilt from upstream sources after loss.
properties.usageExamples: true for derived search index; false for irreplaceable audit originals.

descriptions.en: Whether the data can be rebuilt from upstream sources after loss, e.g. true for a derived search index.
descriptions.cs: Určuje, zda lze data po ztrátě znovu sestavit z upstream zdrojů, např. true u odvozeného search indexu.

properties.usageGuidance: Whether backups are required for this data object.
properties.usageExamples: true for customer master; false for ephemeral cache.

descriptions.en: Whether backups are required for this data object, e.g. true for customer master or false for ephemeral cache.
descriptions.cs: Určuje, zda jsou pro tento datový objekt vyžadovány zálohy, např. true u customer master nebo false u dočasné cache.

properties.usageGuidance: Information security classification of the data.

descriptions.en: Information security classification of the data, e.g. public, internal, confidential, or restricted/PII.
descriptions.cs: Bezpečnostní klasifikace informací, např. public, internal, confidential nebo restricted/PII.

properties.usageGuidance: Runtime environment name for deployed elements.

descriptions.en: Runtime environment name for deployed elements, e.g. prod, staging, test, or dr.
descriptions.cs: Název běhového prostředí nasazených prvků, např. prod, staging, test nebo dr.

properties.usageGuidance: Cluster or platform grouping where the element runs.

descriptions.en: Cluster or platform grouping where the element runs, e.g. k8s-prod-a or esx-cluster-01.
descriptions.cs: Skupina clusteru nebo platformy, kde prvek běží, např. k8s-prod-a nebo esx-cluster-01.

properties.usageGuidance: Logical namespace within a platform (e.g. Kubernetes).

descriptions.en: Logical namespace within a platform, e.g. a Kubernetes namespace like crm-prod.
descriptions.cs: Logický namespace v rámci platformy, např. Kubernetes namespace crm-prod.

properties.usageGuidance: Runtime technology hosting the component.

descriptions.en: Runtime technology hosting the component, e.g. JVM 21, Node 20, or .NET 8.
descriptions.cs: Běhové prostředí hostující komponentu, např. JVM 21, Node 20 nebo .NET 8.

properties.usageGuidance: Configured replica/instance count for capacity and HA reasoning.

descriptions.en: Configured replica or instance count for capacity and high-availability reasoning, e.g. 3 or 2 for active-passive.
descriptions.cs: Nakonfigurovaný počet replik nebo instancí pro kapacitu a HA, např. 3 nebo 2 pro active-passive.

properties.usageGuidance: High-availability pattern in use.

descriptions.en: High-availability pattern in use, e.g. active-active, active-passive, or none.
descriptions.cs: Vzor vysoké dostupnosti, např. active-active, active-passive nebo none.

properties.usageGuidance: Primary operating site for the element.

descriptions.en: Primary operating site for the element, e.g. DC1, eu-central-1a, or Prague.
descriptions.cs: Primární provozní lokalita prvku, např. DC1, eu-central-1a nebo Praha.

properties.usageGuidance: Disaster-recovery site for the element.

descriptions.en: Disaster-recovery site for the element, e.g. DC2, eu-central-1b, or Brno.
descriptions.cs: Lokalita disaster recovery pro prvek, např. DC2, eu-central-1b nebo Brno.

properties.usageGuidance: Where deployment artifacts/config come from.
properties.usageExamples: GitOps repo; CI pipeline; Helm chart registry; manual.

descriptions.en: Where deployment artifacts or configuration come from, e.g. GitOps repo, CI pipeline, or Helm chart registry.
descriptions.cs: Odkud pocházejí deployment artefakty nebo konfigurace, např. GitOps repo, CI pipeline nebo Helm chart registry.

properties.usageGuidance: VLAN identifier for a CommunicationNetwork.

descriptions.en: VLAN identifier for a CommunicationNetwork, e.g. 120 or 900.
descriptions.cs: Identifikátor VLAN pro CommunicationNetwork, např. 120 nebo 900.

properties.usageGuidance: CIDR block of a CommunicationNetwork.

descriptions.en: CIDR block of a CommunicationNetwork, e.g. 10.12.0.0/16 or 192.168.10.0/24.
descriptions.cs: CIDR blok CommunicationNetwork, např. 10.12.0.0/16 nebo 192.168.10.0/24.

properties.usageGuidance: Security or network zone label. Prefer on CommunicationNetwork and Node so flows can be reasoned about by zone; sourceZone/targetZone on Flow should match these labels.

descriptions.en: Security or network zone label used for trust-boundary reasoning, e.g. APP_NET, DB_NET, or DMZ.
descriptions.cs: Označení bezpečnostní nebo síťové zóny pro analýzu trust boundary, např. APP_NET, DB_NET nebo DMZ.

properties.usageGuidance: Site affiliation for network or deployment concepts.

descriptions.en: Site affiliation for network or deployment concepts, e.g. DC1, DC2, or branch-42.
descriptions.cs: Přiřazení k lokalitě u síťových nebo deployment konceptů, např. DC1, DC2 nebo branch-42.

properties.usageGuidance: Routing domain or VRF name for a network.

descriptions.en: Routing domain or VRF name for a network, e.g. corp-prod, pci, or guest.
descriptions.cs: Routing doména nebo název VRF pro síť, např. corp-prod, pci nebo guest.
